t: Entity Identity Graph: a plain-language overview
title: Entity Identity Graph: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Entity Identity Graph does and why archives need it. An entity identity graph answers 'are these all the same person?' It draws a node for every name, ID, or mention, connects the ones that refer to the same entity, and each connected web becomes one identity with one canonical ID. Fifty spellings of one author become one author.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Entity Identity Graph works
title: How the Entity Identity Graph works
description: Overview: what the Entity Identity Graph does and why archives need it. Real identity graphs create nodes for mentions (names, emails, IDs, handles), add edges from alias evidence (same email, fuzzy name match, shared identifier), and compute connected components — each component is one entity. Canonical IDs are minted per component, conflicts (two birth dates in one component) are flagged for review, and new mentions attach to existing components or seed new ones. The graph is the archive's single source of truth for 'who is who'.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Entity Identity Graph works: the deep tour
title: How the Entity Identity Graph works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Entity Identity Graph does and why archives need it. Real identity graphs create nodes for mentions (names, emails, IDs, handles), add edges from alias evidence (same email, fuzzy name match, shared identifier), and compute connected components — each component is one entity. Canonical IDs are minted per component, conflicts (two birth dates in one component) are flagged for review, and new mentions attach to existing components or seed new ones. The graph is the archive's single source of truth for 'who is who'. Advanced graphs weight edges by evidence strength, split components when contradictory evidence arrives (the two John Smiths were different people after all), and propagate corrections through the graph. Quality is measured by component precision/recall on labeled identity corpora. The limits are sparse evidence — a lone mention with no links stays its own component rather than being force-merged — and adversarial identity confusion, which the graph surfaces as low-confidence components instead of hiding.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
